title: Q3 first spend: archive-only recovery hand-back diagnosis
hypothesis: Timed withdrawal of recovery support leaves a transition-associated loss of rolling large enough to make state-dependent hand-back worth testing.

prediction.rationale: Compute the fraction of all archived cases labelled triggered-and-lost-after-hand-back; the comparison is against a zero-prevalence null, not another controller or a treatment-effect estimate. Predict an absolute fraction >=0.06 separately for JOINT in R-124 and R-126. This is twice the later intervention's proposed +0.03 success effect; report the transplant replication separately.

code_changes: Add scripts/recovery_handback_audit.py as one archive-only module; reuse existing recovery_tail_audit.py labelling and interval utilities where available. This implements the archive prerequisite of deferred R-117, not its simulation or training proposal; the earlier R-118 tail audit did not align frozen JOINT/transplant failures to support termination.

Add recovery_handback_archive dispatch to scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and its archive-only configuration to config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml. Dispatch without initializing Isaac or modifying controller assets. Process existing manifests only; no seed is consumed.

Read logs/pen_spin/r124_consolidated_ladder/confirmation/s*/r121_cell.{json,npz}: 24 manifests, 3,072 cases; and logs/pen_spin/r126_block_transplant/confirmation/s*/{joint,transplant}_cell.{json,npz}: 32 manifests, 4,096 cases per controller. Preserve inputs and write a separate audit report with source hashes.

Reconstruct each first-episode trigger at step 149 from centre distance <0.08 and the previous 30 steps' mean absolute axial rate <4.18. Verify indexing and transition timing against the frozen module implementation; align traces to onset, completion of blending at approximately step 184, and boost termination at approximately step 244. Report one-step indexing sensitivity.

For every cell report reconstructed triggers, recorded total triggers, their signed difference and any violation of the recorded-count upper bound. Excess recorded triggers can reflect later auto-reset episodes and must not be presented as a measured per-case mismatch rate. Report reconstruction uncertainty explicitly; aggregate counts cannot certify individual flags.

Before reading case outcomes, freeze the operational labels and windows: at each hand-back boundary, classify dropped, off-centre, rolling above 4 rad/s, or slow using only signals through that boundary and existing audit definitions. Define healthy hand-back conservatively as the archived success predicate true and centre distance <0.08 throughout the preceding 10 steps, including the boundary.

Define the registered reachable subset as reconstructed-triggered, ultimately unsuccessful cases with healthy hand-back at either boundary and the first subsequent predicate loss or recorded drop within the next 30 steps. Count the union once per case. This is a temporal-association screening subset, not proof the loss caused eventual failure or that a hand-back rule could recover it. Report whether rolling subsequently recovers and when intermittent rolling, off-centring and drops begin; retain persistent-slow and intermittent/near-miss labels separately.

Partition remaining failures into untriggered, never re-captured, lost during blending, other pre-boundary losses, later losses outside the registered windows, and ambiguous cases. Do not assume persistent slowness and intermittent failures share a mechanism. Compute case-level and manifest-clustered 95% intervals for all-case fractions separately for R-124 JOINT, R-126 JOINT and R-126 transplant; report 15- and 60-step window sensitivities without replacing the registered 30-step result.

Write gate_statistics containing both JOINT reachable fractions and their uncertainty. Simulation is eligible for a separate agreement only if each JOINT archive has registered reachable mass >=0.06 and reconstruction sensitivity does not invalidate that assessment; discuss transplant concordance explicitly. Below-threshold results close Q3 without a training sweep; unresolved reconstruction leaves it inconclusive. No oracle gate, fitting, controller generation or automatic simulation escalation is permitted.

falsified_by: The registered reachable fraction is below 0.06 in either JOINT archive; an upper 95% interval below 0.06 refutes the predicted magnitude, while an interval spanning 0.06 leaves its magnitude inconclusive. Unresolved trigger-reconstruction ambiguity also makes the diagnosis inconclusive, not grounds for simulation.

definitions.reachable: reconstructed trigger, eventual failure, healthy hand-back at either boundary (the predicate true and the pen centred on each of the preceding steps), first predicate loss or drop within the window
definitions.caveat: a temporal-association screen: not evidence that the loss caused the failure or that a hand-back rule could recover it; trigger flags are reconstructed, not recorded

result.notes: Archive only: no Isaac process, no episode, no model call; labels, windows and the gate were committed (19666343) before the audit read any outcome. Registered screen: failures that follow a healthy hand-back (reconstructed trigger; predicate true and centred on the 10 steps ending at the end of support, step 183, or the end of the stroke boost, step 243; first loss within 30 steps) are 48 of 3,072 JOINT cases in R-124 (0.0156, 95% [0.011, 0.020]) and 67 of 4,096 in R-126 (0.0164 [0.012, 0.020]); the transplant has 40 of 4,096 (0.0098). Both JOINT upper bounds are far below 0.06: REFUTED, and simulation is not eligible. A 60-step window gives 55 and 88 (0.018, 0.021); a 15-step window 38 and 45. Where JOINT's 626 R-124 failures are instead: 239 never triggered (94 early drops, 42 persistent slow, 69 intermittent or near miss, 30 off-centre); 97 triggered and never rolled again after support (63 persistent slow, 31 late drops); 222 triggered and rolled at some point after support but were not rolling steadily at either boundary (147 persistent slow, 63 intermittent or near miss); 20 lost rolling more than 30 steps after a healthy boundary (15 near miss); 48 reachable (28 persistent slow, 19 intermittent or near miss). The same proportions hold in R-126. So the dominant triggered failure is a re-capture that does not produce steady rolling by the time support and boost end, not a good state lost at hand-back; and persistent-slow and intermittent/near-miss failures do not share one cause (near misses are mostly untriggered or late). Reconstruction: 1,191 reconstructed first-episode triggers against 1,236 recorded (which include later auto-reset episodes) in R-124, 1,597 vs 1,658 and 1,545 vs 1,596 in R-126; no cell's reconstruction exceeds its recorded upper bound; moving the window one step later changes 8 trigger flags per archive and the reachable counts by at most 1. Individual flags are reconstructed, not recorded. Excursion from the protocol text, stated in triage: the module is lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/recovery_handback_audit.py (the study registry resolves modules there), not scripts/. Timing was read off the frozen module code: decision at step 149, support 35 steps (boundary index 183), boost 60 steps (boundary index 243). Associations only: nothing here shows what an intervention would recover.

verdicts.reasoning: By the frozen rule: the reachable fraction is 0.0156 [0.011, 0.020] for JOINT in R-124 and 0.0164 [0.012, 0.020] in R-126, both upper bounds far below the 0.06 gate, and still only 0.018-0.021 with a 60-step window; the reconstruction is stable (8 flags change under one-step re-indexing, no cell exceeds its recorded count). A state-dependent hand-back could at most address about 1.6% of cases, half the +0.03 a later intervention would have to register even if it recovered all of them. Per the direction, Q3 closes without a training sweep.
verdicts.next_experiment: Close Q3. The archive points elsewhere: 7.2% of cases trigger and re-capture without reaching steady rolling by the end of support and boost, 3.2% trigger and never roll again, 7.8% fail untriggered (mostly early drops). Move to Q4 (LLM vs grammar construction of the recovery module) with a separately agreed generation budget; R-129's reset-distribution weakness is a separate training-distribution question.

verdicts.reasoning: Against the registered zero-prevalence null—not an empirical controller comparison—the JOINT reachable fractions were 48/3,072 (0.015625) and 67/4,096 (0.016357), both below the predicted 0.06 [logs/pen_spin/r130_handback_audit/summary.json]. Their manifest-clustered 95% intervals were [0.010570, 0.020680] and [0.013377, 0.019338], placing even the upper bounds well below the threshold [logs/pen_spin/r130_handback_audit/summary.json]. The transplant was concordantly below threshold at 40/4,096 (0.009766), with clustered interval [0.006904, 0.012627] [logs/pen_spin/r130_handback_audit/summary.json]. Individual triggers remain reconstructed, but the one-step sensitivity changed JOINT reachable counts to 47 and 67, while the wider 60-step window yielded only 55 and 88, so these reported sensitivities do not overturn the finding [logs/pen_spin/r130_handback_audit/summary.json]. The registered magnitude is therefore refuted and the simulation gate remains closed; this temporal-association screen does not measure an intervention effect [logs/pen_spin/r130_handback_audit/summary.json].

direction: Continue Stage-3 Shadow Hand axial-rolling research from the frozen R-121 JOINT controller. Prioritize independent training reproducibility, then robustness of frozen controllers. Reproduce the successful residual-plus-recovery construction across independent training seeds before claiming a reliable learning algorithm. Evaluate longer horizons and predeclared physical/reset perturbations without fitting. Use archived failures to decide whether recovery hand-back deserves a state-dependent transition study. Then investigate whether LLM-guided construction can discover useful recovery-module structure against grammar search and the hand-designed template under matched budgets. Preserve the original six-second task and evaluation contract. Use JOINT as the experimental reference, preserve all existing assets, and leave default-incumbent installation separate. Run one protocol at a time through the existing advisor/implementer loop. Continue justified follow-ups within this direction; honor its escalation and exhaustion rules. No new global budget ceiling is imposed; each protocol must declare finite simulator, wall-time and model-call costs before agreement. No controller-generation calls for Q1–Q3. Q4 requires a separately agreed generation budget. Advisor calls for the research loop remain permitted throughout.

advisor.reasoning: With Q1 and Q2 completed, this archive-only screen is the right next step to decide whether recovery hand-back warrants a separately agreed intervention. Its weakest point is trigger reconstruction: temporal association cannot establish recoverability, but the protocol explicitly reports ambiguity and blocks simulation escalation when reconstruction is unresolved. Reusing the existing entry point and audit utilities makes the declared cost of zero simulator episodes, zero model calls and 45 minutes justified; the registered threshold and falsification rule make the screen decision-relevant.

implementer.reasoning: Approve: zero-episode, zero-call archive screen with labels, windows and the 0.06 gate fixed before any case outcome is read; it is the direction's required first spend for Q3 and a below-threshold result closes Q3 without a sweep. One implementation note on record, not a design change: the study registry of scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py resolves a study name to a module inside lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin (and scripts never import from other scripts), so the audit module will be lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/recovery_handback_audit.py rather than scripts/recovery_handback_audit.py; everything else as written. I will read the transition timing off the frozen module code (decision at the step whose counter equals round(decision_step), blend from ramp_in and ramp_out, 60 boost steps) rather than the approximate step numbers.
